label: DATING AGAIN

points.heading: Pick a low-pressure plan
points.body: Coffee or a walk feels easier than a long dinner.
points.panel: “Want to grab coffee near the park Saturday?”

points.heading: Breathe before you go in
points.body: A few slow breaths help your body catch up with your plans.
points.panel: Breathe in for four, out for six, three times.

points.heading: Be curious, not perfect
points.body: You’re there to learn about him too, not to pass a test.

points.heading: Notice how you feel
points.body: Ask yourself whether you feel relaxed with him, not just whether he liked you.

points.heading: Be kind to yourself after
points.body: Whatever happens, you showed up. That’s brave.
points.panel: “I did something new, and I’m proud of that.”

close.save: Save this for your next first date.

caption:
First dates after a breakup can feel like learning to ride a bike again: wobbly, exciting, a little scary.

Nerves are normal, and they usually mean you care. These five small steps help you feel calmer, and remember that you’re choosing too. You’re not there to impress. You’re there to find out.
